        fpath = os.path.join\(root, fname\)
        with open\(fpath, ''r'', encoding=''utf-8''\) as f:
            content = f.read\(\)
        
        original = content
        for old, new in replacements.items\(\):
            content = content.replace\(old, new\)
        
        if content != original:
            with open\(fpath, ''w'', encoding=''utf-8''\) as f:
                f.write\(content\)
            changed_files.append\(fpath\)

Bash(git commit -m "$\(cat <<''EOF''
fix: Use lowercase enum names to match PostgreSQL enum values

The Alembic migration created PostgreSQL enums with lowercase values
\(e.g., ''superadmin'', ''available''\), but SQLAlchemy''s Enum\(\) type
persists the Python enum .name \(e.g., ''SUPERADMIN'', ''AVAILABLE''\),
causing insert failures. Fixed by making all enum member names
lowercase to match the database values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
\)")
